pacer: Whitcomb et al. v. InnerChange Chrysalis, LLC et al., No. 9:23-cv-00039 (D. Mont.), docket
lhacase: Lake House Academy v. Jennings (2011), court opinion
preqin: Preqin, Cressey & Company investment record for InnerChange (exit August 2018)
justia24: Whitcomb et al. v. InnerChange Chrysalis, LLC et al., No. 9:23-cv-00039 (D. Mont.), order, Oct 22, 2024

paragraphs: InnerChange was a Utah-based company that owned residential treatment programs, mostly for adolescent girls and young women, from 2006 until 2018.{st06,st13,npi} That year it was folded into Embark Behavioral Health.{st06,st13,npi} It began as Solacium Holdings and was owned in turn by two private equity firms, CIC Partners and Cressey & Company.{tm08,pitch} Its record includes a New Haven therapist, Jason Scott Calder, who pleaded guilty in November 2017 to raping a 16-year-old patient.{sltrib}

The company took shape around two Utah treatment centers.{st06} On July 1, 2006, New Haven, in Spanish Fork, bought Sunrise RTC, and both became part of Solacium Holdings, LLC.{st06} In April 2007 Solacium merged with Wellcore, LLC, which owned Fulshear Ranch Academy in Texas.{wb0507} That August Solacium, then based in Missouri City, Texas, signed a letter of intent to buy Wilderness Quest in Monticello, Utah.{wb1007q} Its chief executive, Val H. Christensen, announced that Alldredge Academy in West Virginia would drop its academic phase and become Alldredge Wilderness Journey.{wb1007q} In October 2007 Woodbury Reports listed Sommerville Young Adult Community, a program for young adults, as part of Solacium Holdings.{wb1007s} Whether the Wilderness Quest purchase closed is not on record; the company's December 2008 list of programs leaves it out.{wb1208} By June 2008 CIC Partners of Dallas owned most of the company, which ran five programs.{tm08} Woodbury Reports announced that June that Anthony Geraci had resigned as Solacium's chief operations and marketing officer and that David Michel would succeed Christensen as president and chief executive.{wb0608} In July 2008 Woodbury gave Solacium's address as Orem, Utah.{wb0708} On November 3, 2008, its chief executive, David Michel, announced that Solacium was now InnerChange.{wb1208} Its programs were New Haven, Sunrise, Fulshear Ranch Academy and Alldredge Wilderness Journey in West Virginia.{wb1208} Alldredge Wilderness Journey closed in 2008.{wb0209} In April 2009 Woodbury listed InnerChange's offices in Addison, Texas.{wb0409} By July 2011 Dustin Tibbitts, New Haven's executive director, was also president of InnerChange.{wb0711} In December 2011 Cressey & Company bought InnerChange from CIC Partners.{pitch}

Under Cressey the company expanded.{st13} In 2011 Lake House Academy in Flat Rock, North Carolina, told a court in a suit against its founder that it was in a prospective sale to InnerChange.{lhacase} On January 2, 2013, it bought Chrysalis in Eureka, Montana, "the fourth facility to join the InnerChange family."{st13} That August, describing itself as "a clinical and operational consulting organization," it began a partnership with the Oakley School in Oakley, Utah.{oak} InnerChange also announced that Paul Taylor, the executive director of Copper Canyon Academy, would become Oakley's executive director.{wb0913} The Oakley School announced in April 2017 that it would close, letting students stay until June 30.{park} In March 2016 Optimum Performance Institute, a residential treatment center in Southern California for people aged 17 to 28, joined.{opi} In August 2018 Calo Programs bought Dragonfly Transitions, a program for young adults in Oregon, from Glen White and Mona Treadway.{hn18} Cressey & Company exited InnerChange that August.{preqin}

In September 2017 the Utah County Sheriff's Office arrested Calder, a licensed therapist who had worked at New Haven.{dn17} Police said he sexually abused a 16-year-old patient during therapy sessions from March to June 2017.{dn17} Co-workers had noticed that his sessions with her ran late at night and included walks off the grounds, which he did not do with other patients.{dn17} He had been fired and was working at another treatment center in Salt Lake County.{dn17} In November 2017 he pleaded guilty to rape, object rape, forcible sodomy, forcible sexual abuse and obstructing justice.{sltrib} In January 2018 he was sentenced to seven years to life in prison.{sltrib}

In October 2018 InnerChange, Calo Programs and two other companies took the shared name Embark Behavioral Health.{st18,npi} New Haven, Sunrise, Chrysalis, Optimum Performance Institute, Vive and Dragonfly Transitions went into Embark under InnerChange, and the name lived on as an Embark division.{st18,npi} Lake House Academy and Fulshear were listed under Calo.{st18} Sunrise is still registered as Solacium Sunrise, LLC, after the company's first name.{npi}

After the merger, in April 2023, Oliver Whitcomb and Amy Clifford sued InnerChange Chrysalis, LLC and others in federal court in Montana, a personal-injury case.{pacer} The suit alleged that a staff member sexually abused students and that other staff members knew of the abuse and allowed it to continue.{justia24} In December 2025 the parties agreed to dismiss it with prejudice; the docket records no judgment on the merits.{pacer}
